instruction: Change Chrome's appearance mode to follow the system theme so it adapts automatically to your OS setting.

parameters.command: mkdir -p /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && if [ ! -f /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences ]; then echo '{}' > /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences; fi && python3 -c "import json; p='/home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences'; d=json.load(open(p)); d.setdefault('browser', {}).setdefault('theme', {})['color_scheme'] = 2; d['browser']['theme']['color_scheme2'] = 2; json.dump(d, open(p, 'w'))"

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully navigated Chrome Settings > Appearance, switched theme to Classic, changed Mode from Dark to Light. Variation requires exactly System Default instead of Light.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Chrome menus, open Settings, modify appearance theme mode dropdown
metadata.explanation: Harder variant: must set mode to System Default (color_scheme=0) not merely Light. The custom getter reads browser.theme.color_scheme and maps it to 'system'/'light'/'dark'. Uses built-in match_in_list metric expecting ['system']. [Fixed: renamed getter function suffix from truncated 'bfb85642' to full 32-char MD5 hash 'c109c66a806aa3929078e7fafeda76b2' computed from '93eabf48-6a27-4cb6-b963-7d5fe1e0d3a9|2'. Old chrome_bfb85642.py cleared of invalid function definition.]
fix_history: Fix 1: Renamed getter file from chrome_bfb85642.py to chrome_c109c66a806aa3929078e7fafeda76b2.py and updated function name to use full 32-char MD5 hash. Updated result.type and new_functions_paths accordingly.
Fix 2: Cleared chrome_bfb85642.py of its invalid 8-char MD5 function 'get_chrome_color_scheme__bfb85642' (replaced with empty placeholder) so rule validator no longer detects the bad suffix.

validation.fix_applied: Cleared chrome_bfb85642.py of invalid function definition; active getter is chrome_c109c66a806aa3929078e7fafeda76b2.py with valid 32-char MD5
llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads browser.theme.color_scheme from Chrome Preferences file and maps {0: 'system', 1: 'light', 2: 'dark'}, directly corresponding to the instruction's requirement.
Metric match_in_list correctly handles expected.type='rule' — receives rules dict {'expected': ['system']} directly and checks result in rules['expected'], which is the correct pattern.
Expected value ['system'] is semantically correct for the instruction (set mode to follow system theme = color_scheme=0).
Negative control resistance is intact: setup initializes color_scheme=2 (dark), so the initial state returns 'dark' which fails the check.
Full instruction coverage: single requirement (system theme mode) is fully verified by the evaluator.
State is read from file (Chrome Preferences), not from live UI, so 1-second postconfig sleep is sufficient to ensure state is persisted.
